comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and overrides),
plus any override added to clear an npm audit advisory. An exact pin is invisible to update-npm-deps.ps1 - that
script upgrades caret ranges and skips exact versions - so nothing would ever remind you a pin is stale. This file
is what makes that check happen: on every run the script executes each `check` and compares its trimmed stdout to
`expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different means the condition that justified the pin has changed
and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no mechanical test exists - it is reported for manual review
on every run instead of going quiet. Every exact pin must have an entry here, and every entry must name a package
that is actually present in the declared section; the script reports either mismatch.

satteri.why: The docs-site mdast plugins import their types from satteri, and the runtime that calls them is the satteri @astrojs/markdown-satteri depends on, which is ^0.11.6 (astro and @astrojs/mdx pin that release). A different satteri here type-checks the plugins against an API the docs build never runs, so the dev copy stays on the release Astro uses. The peer range is ^0.10.5 || ^0.11.6, because Starlight 0.42 still depends on satteri ^0.10.3 directly and a consumer on an older @astrojs/markdown-satteri still runs 0.10; the plugins type-check unchanged against 0.11.
satteri.manualCheck: When the newest @astrojs/markdown-satteri moves to a newer satteri, move this pin, the satteri peer range and @astrojs/markdown-satteri together, and re-run the docs build. Once the peer range drops ^0.10.5, replace the two docs-site `context.setProperty` calls (deprecated in 0.11, which 0.10 needs because it has no `setField`) with `setField` and remove their no-deprecated disables.

fflate.why: Clears GHSA-px8p-9vwx-vf98 (fflate unzipSync infinite loop on a malformed ZIP64 archive, >=0.7.0 <0.7.5). Reached only through satori, whose newest release pins fflate at the exact 0.7.3, so no bump reaches the fix. The override admits 0.7.5 and later; satori calls only inflateSync and zlibSync, which 0.8 keeps. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy: it downgrades satori to 0.32.0.
fflate.manualCheck: The check reads the exact fflate pin of the newest satori. When it reads 0.7.5 or later, drop the override and this entry, and re-run `npm audit`.

katex.why: Clears GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7 (KaTeX trust restrictions bypassed through existing prototype pollution, >=0.11.0 <0.18.2). Reached only through markdownlint -> micromark-extension-math, which declares katex ^0.16.0, so no bump reaches the fix. micromark-extension-math imports katex only in its HTML renderer, which markdownlint never calls (it uses the parser alone), so the forced minor cannot change a lint result. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy: it downgrades markdownlint to 0.36.1.
katex.manualCheck: The check reads the katex range of the newest micromark-extension-math. When it admits 0.18.2 or later, drop the override and this entry once markdownlint's tree resolves to that release, and re-run `npm audit`.

js-yaml.why: Starlight declares js-yaml ^4 and loads it through a default import, which js-yaml 5 (ESM-only, no default export) does not provide, so the tree must stay on 4.x. 4.3.1 and below sit inside GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh; 4.3.2 is the patched release on the v4-legacy dist-tag. The override also holds markdownlint-cli2 below the js-yaml 5 it exact-pins for itself, which works because it only uses the named `load` export, which js-yaml 4 has. The check tracks the v4-legacy dist-tag, because a backport there is the only way an advisory leaves this tree while Starlight is on 4.x.
js-yaml.manualCheck: A newer v4-legacy publish means read its changelog and move this pin onto it. The override can go once nothing needs js-yaml 4, i.e. when `node -e "process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(require('node:fs').readFileSync('node_modules/@astrojs/starlight/package.json','utf8')).dependencies['js-yaml'])"` stops reporting ^4.x. Verify either change with `npm run docs:build` and `npm run lint:md`.

typescript.why: TypeScript 7 (tsgo) breaks this toolchain: @typescript-eslint's parser crashes on the native API, so type-aware ESLint cannot run on 7. @typescript-eslint peer-requires the range below, so 6.x is the last usable major. Propagates to the whole tree via overrides.typescript = $typescript.

glob.why: Clears GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 (glob >=9.0.0 <=14.0.1, fixed in 14.0.2) and, with it, GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 on the minimatch 9 and 10 that glob 10 and 13 nest. jest 30 (@jest/reporters, jest-config, jest-runtime) declares glob ^13 and test-exclude 7 declares glob ^10, and each calls only the named glob / globSync exports, which glob 14 keeps. Replace glob itself rather than the minimatch under it: glob 10 and 13 read Minimatch.set, which minimatch 11 changes. Caret because it is an advisory floor.
glob.manualCheck: Remove the override when jest-config and test-exclude admit glob >=14.0.2, then reinstall and rerun npm audit and the jest integration test (src/jest-runner.integration.test.ts).

eslint-plugin-tsdoc.why: A nested override, { "minimatch": "^11.0.5" }, clearing GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 (minimatch <11.0.1) for the copy under eslint-plugin-tsdoc alone. eslint-plugin-tsdoc 0.5.4 pins @typescript-eslint/utils ~8.56.0, whose typescript-estree 8.56.1 keeps minimatch 10 and calls only minimatch(filePath, pattern, { dot: true }), which minimatch 11 keeps. Scoped rather than global because typedoc 0.28.20 calls Minimatch#set with matchOne, which minimatch 11 removed.
eslint-plugin-tsdoc.manualCheck: Remove the override when eslint-plugin-tsdoc moves to a typescript-eslint that takes minimatch 11, then reinstall and rerun npm audit and npm run lint.

@stryker-mutator/core.why: A nested override, { "minimatch": "^11.0.5" }, clearing GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 for @stryker-mutator/core alone, which declares minimatch ~10.2.4 and calls only minimatch() and new Minimatch().match(), which minimatch 11 keeps. Scoped for typedoc's reason (see eslint-plugin-tsdoc).
@stryker-mutator/core.manualCheck: Remove the override when @stryker-mutator/core admits minimatch >=11.0.1, then reinstall and rerun npm audit and npm run test:mutation on one module.

test-exclude.why: A nested override, { "minimatch": "^11.0.5" }, clearing GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 for test-exclude 7 (through jest's babel-plugin-istanbul), which declares minimatch ^10.2.2 and calls only minimatch(), which minimatch 11 keeps. Scoped for typedoc's reason (see eslint-plugin-tsdoc).
test-exclude.manualCheck: Remove the override when test-exclude admits minimatch >=11.0.1, then reinstall and rerun npm audit and the jest integration test.

eslint-plugin-import-x.why: A nested override, { "minimatch": "^11.0.5" }, so eslint-plugin-import-x, whose range ^9.0.3 || ^10.1.2 || ^11.0.1 otherwise dedupes onto the root minimatch 10 typedoc holds, takes a patched copy for GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249. It calls only the named minimatch(), which minimatch 11 keeps.
eslint-plugin-import-x.manualCheck: Remove the override once typedoc takes minimatch 11 (T6738 upstream) and the root minimatch is 11, then reinstall and rerun npm audit and npm run lint.
